props.gloss_en: R' Yochanan: the etrog on the seventh day is forbidden
R' Yochanan: on the eighth it is permitted
R' Yochanan: the sukkah, even on the eighth, is forbidden
Reish Lakish: the etrog, even on the seventh, is permitted
the stam: they dispute how far the etrog was set aside -- for its mitzva, or for the whole day
the etrog was set aside [only] for its mitzva
the etrog was set aside for the whole day
the mishna: immediately [after the mitzva] children remove their lulavim and eat their etrogim
no: the mishna speaks of children specifically
the same holds even for adults; the mishna says 'children' because it states the usual case

Abaye: the sukkah is fit for use at twilight (should a meal come his way he must sit and eat in it), so it is set aside for twilight, and since it is set aside for twilight it is set aside for the whole eighth day
Abaye: the etrog is not fit for use at twilight, so it is not set aside for twilight nor for the whole eighth day
Levi: the etrog is forbidden even on the eighth
Avuha diShmuel: the etrog is forbidden on the seventh
Avuha diShmuel: on the eighth it is permitted
Avuha diShmuel came to stand by Levi's view
R' Zeira stood by Avuha diShmuel's view
R' Zeira: an etrog that became unfit may not be eaten all seven [days]
R' Zeira: a person should not give a child ownership of the hoshana on the first Festival day
the stam: because a child acquires but cannot transfer ownership, and [the adult] ends up fulfilling with a lulav not his own
R' Zeira: a person should not tell a child 'I will give you something' and then not give it
R' Zeira: because he comes to teach him falsehood
R' Zeira: as it is said, 'they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood' (Yirmeyahu 9:4)
the stam: Rav and Rav Asi dispute in the dispute of R' Yochanan and Reish Lakish -- the extent to which the etrog was set aside
Rav: one who designated seven etrogim for seven days fulfills with each and eats it immediately
Rav Asi: he fulfills with each and eats it the next day
Abaye: on the eighth that may be the seventh, [the etrog] is forbidden
Abaye: on the ninth that may be the eighth, it is permitted
Mareimar: even on the eighth that may be the seventh, it is permitted
in Sura they acted as Mareimar
Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi acted as Abaye
and the halakha follows Abaye
Rav: the eighth that may be the seventh counts as the seventh for the sukkah
Rav: and as the eighth for the blessing
R' Yochanan: as the eighth for this and for that -- for the sukkah
R' Yochanan: as the eighth for this and for that -- for the blessing
on the eighth that may be the seventh, we sit in the sukkah
on the eighth that may be the seventh, we do not sit in the sukkah either
we also recite the blessing [over sitting in the sukkah]
we do not recite the blessing
Rav Yosef: hold R' Yochanan's [view] in your hand
Rav Huna bar Bizna and all the great of the generation happened to be in a sukkah on the eighth that may be the seventh: they sat, and did not bless
the master of the teaching, Rav Yehuda son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, himself sat outside the sukkah on the eighth that may be the seventh
R' Yochanan: one says the blessing of time on the eighth of the Festival
R' Yochanan: and one does not say it on the seventh of Pesach
know [that this is so]: the eighth is distinct in three things -- sukkah, lulav and the water libation
R' Yehuda: he would pour [the water libation] with a log all eight [days]
and for R' Yehuda, it is distinct in two things
the master said: [eating matza] the first night is obligatory, from then on optional
Ravina: this [the eighth of Sukkot] is distinct from the day before it
Ravina: and that [the seventh of Pesach] is distinct only from the day before the day before it
(Rav Pappa): here (the eighth) 'a bull' is written, there 'bulls'
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: here 'on the day' is written, there 'and on the day'
Rav Ashi: here 'according to the ordinance' is written, there 'according to their ordinance'
the baraita: the bulls, the rams and the lambs are indispensable to one another
R' Yehuda: the bulls are not indispensable to one another
R' Yehuda: for they diminish progressively
R' Yehuda: the eighth is a Festival by itself
R' Yehuda: as the seven days of the Festival require an offering, song and blessing, so the eighth requires offering, song and blessing
R' Yehuda: and the eighth, like the seven, requires lodging [overnight in Jerusalem]
the stam: no -- the 'blessing' is Grace after Meals and the prayer
Rav Nachman: the blessing of time may be said even in the marketplace
R' Yehuda: Pesach Sheni does not require lodging
R' Yehuda: as it is said 'and you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents' (Devarim 16:7), and it is written 'six days you shall eat matzot' (Devarim 16:8)
R' Yehuda: what requires six [days] requires lodging; what does not require six does not require lodging
the stam: no -- it comes to exclude Pesach Sheni, which is like [the first Pesach]
the mishna: first fruits require an offering, song, waving and lodging
the stam: whom have you heard say [first fruits require] waving? R' Yehuda -- and [the mishna] says they require lodging
R' Yehuda: 'and you shall set it down' (Devarim 26:10) is waving -- since setting down is already said in 'and he shall set it down' (Devarim 26:4)
R' Eliezer ben Yaakov: 'and the priest shall take the basket from your hand' (Devarim 26:4) teaches that first fruits require waving
the stam: how so? the priest places his hand under the owner's hand and waves
Rav Nachman: one says the blessing of time on the eighth of the Festival
Rav Sheshet: one does not say the blessing of time on the eighth of the Festival
the baraita: the eighth is a Festival by itself for lottery, the blessing of time, festival, offering, song and blessing

schemas.gloss_en: אתיא יד יד משלמים: 'ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך' (Devarim 26:4) and 'ידיו תביאינה את אשי ה׳' (Vayikra 7:30) -- first fruits require waving as the peace-offering does
מה כאן כהן, אף להלן כהן -- as with first fruits a priest [waves], so with the peace-offering
ומה להלן בעלים, אף כאן בעלים -- as with the peace-offering the owner [waves], so with first fruits

supports.gloss_en: דאמר רבי זירא: אתרוג שנפסלה אסור לאוכלה כל שבעה -- it remains set aside through all seven
version 1: the great of the generation sat and did not bless -- so the blessing is not said (a maaseh; SupportKind has no maaseh member)

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודלמא סבירא להו כמאן דאמר: כיון שבירך יום טוב ראשון שוב אינו מברך? -- perhaps they did not bless because they had blessed on the first day

refuted_by.gloss_en: גמירי דמאפר אתו -- it is known by tradition they had come from the field [and had not sat in a sukkah before]

supports.gloss_en: version 2: the master of the teaching himself sat outside the sukkah -- so Rav's teaching cannot mean we sit
תדע -- the eighth is distinct in three things, so it is a Festival of its own

deflected_by.gloss_en: אי הכי, שביעי של פסח נמי הרי חלוק באכילת מצה! (דאמר מר: לילה ראשונה חובה, מכאן ואילך רשות) -- distinctness would give the seventh of Pesach זמן too

refuted_by.gloss_en: הכי השתא? התם -- מלילה חלוק, מיום אינו חלוק; הכא -- אפילו מיום נמי חלוק

supports.gloss_en: Ravina's distinction (another answer to 47a.6's אי הכי): the eighth differs from the day before it; the seventh of Pesach only from the day before the day before
לימא מסייע ליה ... אף שמיני טעון ... ברכה -- מאי לאו זמן? the 'blessing' the eighth requires would be the blessing of time
הכי נמי מסתברא, דאי סלקא דעתך זמן -- זמן כל שבעה מי איכא? the seven are said to require the blessing, and the blessing of time is not said all seven

deflected_by.gloss_en: הא לא קשיא: דאי לא בריך האידנא -- מברך למחר, או ליומא אחרינא

supports.gloss_en: מכל מקום כוס בעינן! -- even blessing on another day, [the blessing of time] needs a cup, and is there a cup every day?

deflected_by.gloss_en: דלמא דאיקלע ליה כוס -- perhaps a cup happened to be available to him

supports.gloss_en: לימא מסייע ליה לרב נחמן: דאי אמרת בעינן כוס, כוס כל יומא מי איכא?

deflected_by.gloss_en: דלמא דאיקלע ליה כוס -- the baraita need not mean it is said without a cup

supports.gloss_en: הכי נמי מסתברא, דתנן: הביכורים טעונין ... לינה -- and that mishna is R' Yehuda's (p_bikkurim_kerabbi_yehuda), so his rule does not exclude everything lacking six days

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודלמא רבי אליעזר בן יעקב היא -- the mishna may be R' Eliezer ben Yaakov's, who also holds first fruits require waving

supports.gloss_en: דתניא, רבי יהודה אומר: והנחתו -- זו תנופה
תניא כוותיה דרב נחמן: שמיני רגל בפני עצמו לענין פז״ר קש״ב -- זמן בפני עצמו

objections.gloss_en: איתיביה ריש לקיש לרבי יוחנן: מיד תינוקות שומטין את לולביהן ואוכלין אתרוגיהן -- מאי לאו הוא הדין לגדולים? the same should hold for adults' etrogim, so the etrog is permitted on the seventh
איכא דאמרי, איתיביה רבי יוחנן לריש לקיש: מיד התינוקות שומטין... תינוקות -- אין, גדולים -- לא! (in this version R' Yochanan objects)

answered_by.gloss_en: הוא הדין דאפילו גדולים, והאי דקתני תינוקות -- אורחא דמילתא קתני (Reish Lakish's answer in this version; = p_orcha_dmilta)

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רב פפא לאביי: לרבי יוחנן, מאי שנא סוכה, מאי שנא אתרוג? why is the sukkah forbidden on the eighth while the etrog is permitted?

answered_by.gloss_en: the sukkah is fit at twilight and so set aside for it and, מיגו, for the whole eighth; the etrog is not fit at twilight (= p_abaye_sukkah_bein_hashmashot, p_abaye_etrog_lo_chazi)

objections.gloss_en: אמרו לו: והלא כולן מתמעטין והולכין בשמיני! -- all of them [rams and lambs too] diminish on the eighth

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר להן: שמיני רגל בפני עצמו הוא (= p_yehuda_regel_bifnei_atzmo)

objections.gloss_en: וסבר רבי יהודה שמיני טעון לינה? והתניא... את שאינו טעון ששה אינו טעון לינה. למעוטי מאי? לאו למעוטי נמי שמיני של חג?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, למעוטי פסח שני דכוותיה (= p_lemaatei_pesach_sheni)

rulings.gloss_en: והלכתא: אומרים זמן בשמיני של חג
